trust_decision.summary: Whether a Vault address (and TLS skip-verify) taken from an untrusted object annotation may be used by the webhook's own Vault client, and before a ServiceAccount token is minted; decided in newVaultClient using a provenance flag set by parseVaultConfig.

landing_point.why: newVaultClient is where the annotation address becomes clientConfig.Address and where the SA token is minted (webhook.go:285), so an engineer reading 'webhook makes outbound call to attacker URL ... TokenRequest' goes here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: same four admission routes via parseVaultConfig; value also injected into pods as VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY (pod.go:93-94, pod.go:333-334)

fix_sites.module_kind: defaults (new operator knobs vault_addr_allowlist, vault_allow_object_skip_verify, vault_allow_private_addr)
handler-level client constructor (validation via common.ValidateObjectAddr before connect/token mint)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/webhook/config.go:107-111 (annotation-vs-operator-default merge must record provenance; operator default vault_addr implicitly allowlisted, fix.diff:62-64)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The parser 'just reads annotations' and the address is legitimately injected into pods unchanged (pod.go:89-90), so a solver can argue the only place to touch is the client constructor and that skip-verify is a separate, documented user feature (deploy/charts/vault-secrets-webhook/README.md:18).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An object-supplied vault-addr must still be injected verbatim into mutated pods (pods connect themselves) and an allowlisted or operator-default address must still work from Secrets/ConfigMaps; in-cluster hostnames are not DNS-resolved. Rejecting the annotation in the parser or blocking all hostnames/private IPs breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: annotation equal to operator default (implicitly allowed)
skip-verify annotation true without operator opt-in

O7_producer.where: pkg/webhook/config.go:94-111 (parseVaultConfig produces Addr and, after fix, AddrFromObject)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: registry-skip-verify annotation is honoured from the object without operator opt-in and disables TLS on the webhook's outbound registry fetch during admission
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different feature (image registry lookup, not Vault) and the advisory names only vault-addr/vault-skip-verify
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, other file: pkg/webhook/registry.go:185-188 via pod.go:279

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a legacy/alias annotation key (e.g. old vault.security.banzaicloud.io vs new prefix) that also sets Addr but not the provenance flag
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Projects that renamed annotation prefixes keep fallback lookups; the provenance flag must be set at every producer, a how-type miss.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second Vault client constructor (e.g. a transit/agent-config helper) that builds vaultapi config from VaultConfig.Addr without calling the guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Three mutators already construct clients; a maintainer adding a lightweight client for one mutator could bypass newVaultClient.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a vault-addr carried in the referenced TLS secret or a configmap and applied to the webhook client
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Annotation values already pull data from Secrets in webhook.go:213-234, making a config-from-secret address a plausible extension.

O9_family: SSRF (CWE-918) with object-controlled TLS verification bypass and credential (SA token) exfiltration

O10_build.project_tests: pkg/webhook/webhook_test.go (TestNewVaultClientMetrics uses fake clientset), pkg/common/addr_test.go, pkg/common/policy_test.go; e2e/ needs a cluster

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Call common.ValidateObjectAddr on every vaultConfig.Addr in newVaultClient (rejecting the operator default when no allowlist is set) or reject the annotation in parseVaultConfig, and leave vault-skip-verify untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Pod image references cause outbound registry fetches to arbitrary hosts with pod pull secrets (pkg/webhook/registry.go:191-196); separate design question, not pursued.
vault-tls-secret annotation lets an object choose any Secret in the webhook namespace as Vault CA (pkg/webhook/config.go:153-154, pkg/webhook/webhook.go:213-234); not pursued.
vault-serviceaccount annotation still lets an object mint a token for any SA in its own namespace toward the trusted Vault (pkg/webhook/webhook.go:259-296); fix does not change this.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo inferred from 23 Go source files in the tree.

The guard helpers (pkg/common/addr.go, pkg/common/policy.go) already exist at the pinned commit (parent commit 71cfbb8 added them), which makes the fix largely wiring and hands the solver the mechanism.
